Every render site shows it as a shield, and Iron Buckler IS a shield, so a player recognises the object correctly and would not name it as something else; the failure mode this audit is for (wrong reference class) did not happen. The "indistinguishable from Iron Shield" claim also does not hold up: iron_shield__painted has a thin, low-contrast dark cross on a dark face and reads as a plain shield at small size, while iron_buckler carries a big pale-rimmed circular boss covering roughly a third of the face — that disc is the single strongest value break in the picture and survives downscaling far better than the cross does. The same convention runs consistently across bronze/steel/mithril/cobalt/starsteel/voidsteel bucklers (all heater + prominent central boss), so within the game's own visual language "big round centre" already reads as the buckler line. What is genuinely true is that the shape word lost to the shield prior: "a small round buckler" was appended after "A single shield seen face on", and Turbo answered the leading noun. If this family is ever regenerated, drop the word "shield" entirely and lead with the shape — one small round metal disc, flat circular rim, single domed knob at the dead centre, dull grey iron — since keeping "shield" first guarantees the heater outline again. Not worth a reroll on its own.

confirms.depicts: A flat cobalt-blue cross glyph: a tapered point at the top, a wide horizontal crossguard at the vertical centre, and a second limb below the guard that is the same width as the blade and tapers to a matching point at the bottom.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is the same defect in BOTH files, so it is not a variant-selection issue. Measured on the painted PNG (ink y6-y121): blade runs y6 to the guard at y50 = 44px; guard y50-y68 (peak 54px wide); below it a second flare y70-y80 (up to 40px), a straight 24px shaft y82-y104, then a taper 22px->4px ending in a POINT at y121 = 53px of handle. Emblem is the same: blade 48px, handle 56px, also pointed. So the handle is longer than the blade and identical in width to it, and the two tapers are near-equal (20px top vs 17px bottom) — downsampled to 16px the painted file is an almost perfect mirror about the crossguard. Cross-checked cobalt_sword__emblem: its guard sits 9 rows down out of 14 with a blunt grip end, which reads correctly as a sword; the dagger has none of that asymmetry. I softened one thing from the first pass — there IS a shaft below the guard, so "no grip" is overstated, and the crossguard plus blade point does still signal "bladed weapon", so a player will not mistake it for a non-weapon item. That is why I kept severity at weak rather than wrong-object. But it does not read as a DAGGER (short blade is the whole point of the silhouette) and it is not distinguishable from the sword at satchel size. Prompt cause: the current prompt asks for "no crossguard, small round pommel" — the negative did nothing and the pommel never rendered, leaving a bare taper. Suggested rewrite, subject sentence only: "A single short upright knife whose stubby leaf shaped blade takes up only the top third of the picture, below it a wide flat oval guard, then a long dark wrapped grip that ends in a fat heavy round ball at the very bottom, the bottom end blunt and rounded and wider than the grip, deep vivid cobalt blue."

confirms.depicts: A blue heater shield seen face on, pointed at the bottom, with a large dark navy ring boss at its centre containing a pale sky-blue dome. Bright luminous mithril blue with a darker rim.
confirms.note: The first pass described the picture correctly but I don't think it's a defect. Three checks: (1) It reads unambiguously as a shield, and a buckler IS a shield-class offhand -- category is right. (2) The luminous sky blue matches the rest of the mithril family, so tier is right. (3) I pulled mithril_shield__painted.png to test the "same silhouette as the other shields in the tier" claim. The silhouette is shared, but the central marks are not: the buckler has a bold dark navy ring boss over roughly a third of the face, the shield has a pale quartering cross. Those are large, high-contrast, differently-valued shapes -- exactly the kind that survives a 15-20px downscale -- so a player with both in the satchel can tell them apart. Shared silhouette with a swapped central detail is also the documented house style for tiered families, not an accident. What's left is that a buckler is technically a small round shield and this is a heater. That's a geometry pedantry a player will never act on; they see a blue shield under the label "Mithril Buckler", equip it, and move on. Doesn't meet the bar of not recognising the item or reading it as something else. Worth recording for whenever the shield line does get redrawn: the prompt opens with "A single shield seen face on", and per the noun-prior rule that leading noun is what Turbo answered -- "a small round buckler" sitting third could never win. A real round buckler needs the word "shield" removed entirely and the shape stated positively and first, e.g. "A single small round metal disc held on the arm, one raised dome at its dead centre, riveted rim, circular all the way round with no point at the bottom". Same fix applies to iron_buckler and the other seven bucklers, which all share this prompt template.

confirms.depicts: A violet-and-silver pointed heater shield seen face on, with a large white eight-point starburst across the centre — the same body, rim and pointed base as the Starsteel Shield tile, differing only in the centre motif.
confirms.note: Genuine defect, not over-flagging. A buckler is defined by being small and round; this is a full heater shield with a pointed base, and it is a near-duplicate of starsteel_shield__painted.png in the same set (identical silhouette, identical palette, only the star motif differs — 4-point vs 8-point, which is one indistinct white blob at 15px). Player reads it as a shield, which is not wrong at the family level, hence weak rather than wrong-object; but in the gear grid the buckler and shield tiles cannot be told apart, so the name is contradicted and one of the two items is effectively unlabelled. Cause is the prompt: it opens with the noun "shield", so Turbo answered with its heater prior and dropped the trailing "small round buckler" qualifier. Fix by removing the word shield entirely rather than qualifying it. Suggested rewrite: "A single small round disc of pale violet white metal seen face on, its outline a perfect circle, a domed knob bulging from the exact centre, a plain rolled rim running all the way around the edge, a few rivet studs spaced around that rim, the whole disc flat and wide with nothing hanging below it." Also worth differentiating the centre motif from starsteel_shield at the same time.

confirms.depicts: A chestnut red-brown blocky maul head on a long thin diagonal haft — a war hammer / maul, correctly matching "Chitin Maul".
confirms.note: Not a defect. The shipping pick is the emblem variant (picks.json:287, chosen deliberately over painted), and it is exactly what the prompt asked for: "one glossy chestnut chitin block on a long haft". I flattened it on the panel colour and viewed it at 18px and at 512px. At 18px the silhouette is unmistakably a big blocky head on a haft — a maul. No player calls that anything other than a hammer, which is the correct object class, so it fails neither the wrong-object nor the unreadable test. The first pass's complaints are material nitpicks, not identification failures: (1) "reads as a wooden mallet" — at 15-20px no icon in this library conveys surface microtexture, and the chestnut red-brown is the same family colour as chitin_boots / chitin_chest / chitin_legs on the same sheet, so the palette actually does the chitin signalling by association; (2) "tilted off-axis" — the diagonal haft is what separates it from the vertical Bronze Hammer and makes it legible as a distinct entry rather than a recolour. Genuine but minor: the head sits small in the frame versus Bronze Hammer's, and there is a small round nub at the head's upper-left corner that serves no purpose (harmless — it reads as part of the head, not a second object). Worth flagging for whoever touches this later: do NOT swap to chitin_maul__painted.png. That variant is a full noun-prior failure — "war hammer" produced an armoured humanoid figure holding a pole diagonally across its body, a person not a weapon. The emblem is the good one and should stay.

confirms.depicts: A matched pair of bronze leg armour plates standing upright side by side: a flared riveted thigh plate at the top, a large domed knee cop at the joint in the middle, and a tapering shin plate below ending in a straight cut edge. Warm brown-gold bronze, strong specular highlights, dark outline.
confirms.note: Not confirmed. The painted variant (the one picks.json selects) is a legitimate articulated leg harness — cuisse, poleyn, greave — mirrored as a pair. The first pass read the central dome as a decorative boss on an arm cuff, but a large dome at the mid-joint of a paired vertical limb piece is a knee cop, which is specifically leg-armour anatomy; arm cuffs are drawn singly or crossed, not as a mirrored upright pair. The "open-ended straight bottom" it objected to is exactly what the prompt specified, and it is what distinguishes Legs from Boots in this library. Rendered at 18px beside bronze_gloves, bronze_boots and iron_legs, bronze_legs stays clearly separate: gloves collapse to one diagonal blob, boots show a foot flare, and bronze_legs is a blocky paired vertical with a mid break. There is also no vambrace or bracer item anywhere in the game, so the misread the first pass proposes has no competing item to land on. Worth noting the opposite way round: iron_legs and steel_legs draw full harnesses with feet, which overlap the boots icon, so bronze_legs is the more correct of the three. Contrast and silhouette are strong; nothing to fix here.

confirms.depicts: A pair of tall glossy chestnut-brown leg guards standing upright side by side, rounded knee cups at the top, long shin plates tapering down to small rounded ends at the ankle.
confirms.note: Not confirmed. Item is "Chitinweave Chaps" and the icon plainly shows paired leg armour. I re-rendered it beside chitin_boots and bronze_legs at 15/20/31px on a dark satchel ground (scratchpad/cmp_legs.png): the chaps are two narrow vertical bars with a visible gap spanning nearly the full frame height, while the boots are a single compact wide bottom-heavy mass with the classic shaft-plus-sole L profile. Aspect ratio and mass distribution separate them at 15px before colour is even a factor. The bottoms do round off slightly instead of the flat cut edge the prompt asked for, but they read as ankle ends, not feet — there is no sole, no toe, no boot cuff. The silhouette also matches the game's own established legs language: Bronze Legs on the same sheet is the same paired-guards-with-knee-cups shape and coexists with Bronze Boots without confusion. This is a minor fidelity quibble at most, not a misread.

confirms.depicts: A single dagger seen diagonally, blade pointing down-right: tapered light-grey blade with a darker central fuller, a chunky dark crossguard and a round ball pommel, all in a heavy black outline. The emblem variant is the same dagger in cooler blue-grey with a more visible crossguard. Clean, isolated, one object filling the frame.
confirms.note: NOT CONFIRMED - do not regenerate. The first pass's observation is factually correct and I verified it by counting pixels: both files contain exactly ZERO warm pixels (r-b > 30) out of 4468 opaque px painted / 3931 emblem, max warmth 2 and 0. The prompt's "trailing sparks" was dropped completely and "ash grey" rendered as cool bluish steel. (By contrast moltensteel_dagger, prompt "black iron cracked with glowing orange", came back a fully saturated orange blade - the model does honour ember when it takes it.) However, that is a missing-flavour problem, not a failed depiction. Cinderfang IS a dagger and the icon is an unmistakable dagger: bold diagonal silhouette, 35% of opaque pixels are pure black outline, strong value contrast, reads well at 15px. No player would fail to recognise it or call it a different object, which is the bar for confirmation. Real but minor cost: the library holds 15 daggers and the named uniques (Starfang, Voidrend, Plague Fang, Cinderfang) are distinguished by colour treatment alone, so Cinderfang forfeits its identifying mark - though its diagonal ball-pommel composition does not actually collide with steel_dagger's vertical broad blade or iron_dagger's. Severity marked weak to describe it honestly as identifiable-but-plain, not as a defect needing a re-roll. If a future ember pass ever sweeps the uniques, the fix is to lead the prompt with the glow as the subject ("a dagger whose blade is dark ash grey shot through with glowing orange embers along the edge") rather than trailing "trailing sparks" at the end where cfg 2.4 discards it.

confirms.depicts: A single all-metal sledgehammer in tarnished grey-green: a chunky angled block head sitting on top of a vertical shaft, a rounded pommel knob at the base, and an extra curved crescent-shaped lobe fused to the left of the shaft below the head.
confirms.note: First pass is mistaken on its central claim. Measured on the painted PNG (128x128, object bbox x36-91 y6-121), the top-third block head is 32.7% of opaque pixels and the left crescent lobe is 22.0% - the head is ~1.5x the crescent, not "small" beside a "large" blade, and it does not dominate. The head is 40px wide against a 20px shaft, forming a clear T at the top, which is the silhouette cue that decides the read. The crescent is fused mid-shaft BELOW the head, whereas axe geometry puts the bit at the very top flaring off the haft. Rendered the real axes for comparison (iron_axe, steel_axe, bronze_axe, family=tools): all three are wide horizontal heads - two double-bit - on BROWN WOODEN hafts, while this is monochrome green end to end, so colour alone separates them at satchel size. Downsampled to 15/20/31px it holds as "block on a stick with a lump on the side" - a hammer with a beard or flange, not a hatchet. Against its own tier ladder (iron/steel/bronze/runite hammer) it shares the narrow-shaft-plus-top-block silhouette; it is noisier than iron and steel but far more legible than runite_hammer, which is a genuinely malformed green blob and is the icon on this ladder actually worth flagging. The crescent is an unrequested Turbo artefact and mildly untidy, but it does not change the object class and no player would identify this as an axe.

confirms.depicts: A sleeveless soft brown leather jerkin, hollow and empty, with X-lacing down the front and a buckled waist belt. Chestnut/orange-brown throughout, no scales or plating.
confirms.note:
CONFIRMED, but the cause is an authoring bug rather than a Turbo miss. In audit-05.json chitin_plate's prompt is a verbatim copy of chitin_chest's: "A single sleeveless leather jerkin, laced front, hollow and empty, glossy chestnut brown chitin". The generator was never asked for a plate, and the image (picks.json:298 selects "emblem") faithfully renders that wrong prompt. It contradicts the item's own data: cindervale.html:8815 says "Overlapping spider-plate scales stitched with silk... faint violet sheen", and the legacy SVG at line 11877 is deep purple (#3a1868/#7858a8) with rows of scale plates. The new art is brown soft leather with lacing - it reads as the Roughhide/Chitinweave leather line, not the brood-matron plate drop.

Downgrading the first pass's duplicate claim: the files are NOT pixel-identical (chitin_plate has X-lacing, chitin_chest has horizontal frog toggles; indistinguishable below ~30px but not the same image), and chitin_chest appears exactly ONCE in cindervale.html - line 36010, the art map only, with no name/stats/slot/drop entry. It is not a live item, so players cannot currently see the two together. The "two chest items cannot be told apart" part of the reason is not a live defect; the wrong-subject part is.

Severity weak not wrong-object: at 15-20px the silhouette still reads as chest-slot body armour, which is the correct class - it just fails to say "chitin plate".

Suggested replacement subject sentence (drops the "leather jerkin" prior that produced the soft cloth, states absence positively, gives concrete shape):
"A single hard chest breastplate built from four rows of overlapping curved beetle shell segments, deep violet purple with a glossy sheen, flared wide at the shoulders and narrowing at the waist, hollow and empty with no head, no arms and nobody wearing it."

confirms.depicts: An orange-headed mallet sitting inside an opaque black rounded-square plaque. At 15-20px the plaque dominates and the icon reads as a dark tile with an orange sliver in it, not as a war hammer.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is a keying failure rather than a generation failure. picks.json selects `painted`, so slagbreaker__painted.png is what ships. Alpha probe: 59.3% of the frame is opaque and 84.1% of that opaque area is near-black (luma <45) — half the whole image is an opaque black mass, with transparent corners proving it is a rounded-square plaque rather than a keying near-miss. Rendered at true size beside iron_hammer, steel_hammer and soulbinder_hammer, all three siblings float clean on the tile with readable silhouettes at 15px while slagbreaker is a black box with a thin orange mark; the defect is unmistakable in A/B. I do NOT confirm the first pass's second claim about the head reading as a paddle/spatula — at 96px it is a square block on a long haft, near-identical in silhouette to soulbinder_hammer, which reads fine. The plaque is the entire problem. Cheapest fix: the emblem variant of this same id is already keyed correctly (12.1% opaque, 0% dark-opaque), so flipping picks.json slagbreaker from "painted" to "emblem" fixes it with no regeneration, at the cost of a plainer flat-orange shape. If regenerating instead, note the likely cause: "glowing orange slag block" makes the model paint a dark contrast surround behind the glow, and that surround is dense enough to survive the key. Describe the heat as being in the metal rather than as a glow, e.g. "A single war hammer, one thick rectangular iron head with a flat striking face at the top of a long straight haft, the head streaked with veins of cooling orange molten slag."

confirms.depicts: A bright vermilion and orange heater-shaped shield with a dark rim, faceted panels radiating from a dark round boss at the centre; the emblem variant is a near-black shield with a glowing orange ring at its centre.
confirms.note: The shape observation is accurate but does not amount to a failure. The icon depicts a shield, the item is a shield, and no player would name it as a different object; buckler-vs-heater is a nomenclature nuance invisible at 15-20px. The duplication claim does not hold on inspection: moltensteel_shield is near-black with a large glowing orange horned-creature emblem, while the buckler is bright red-orange with a plain round central boss, so the two separate on both dominant value and central mark even at grid size. Silhouette is bold and contrast is strong, which is what actually matters at this size. Worth logging separately as a set-wide cosmetic point (all ten bucklers rendered as heaters): the prompt leads with "A single shield seen face on, raised boss at its centre" and Turbo answers that clause before reaching "a small round buckler". If a round shape is wanted, drop the word shield and lead with the geometry, e.g. "A single small circular hand guard of metal, perfectly round, one raised dome at its centre, a studded rim all the way around" plus the colour phrase.

confirms.depicts: A single brown leather glove, palm forward, four fingers up and thumb across, with a wide cuff at the wrist, dark outline and cuff highlight.
confirms.note: Both first-pass objections fail on inspection. (1) The "Bracers vs glove" mismatch is a game-wide naming convention, not an art defect: cindervale.html:26074 sets _LSLOT_NOUN={helm:'Cowl',chest:'Jerkin',legs:'Chaps',gloves:'Bracers',boots:'Boots'}, so all 10 LEATHER_TIERS sets name their gloves-slot piece "<Set> Bracers". The item id is chitin_gloves, slot is gloves, generator is gen:'gloves'. The player equips it to the hands slot and sees a hand covering — correct. Confirming this would condemn all ten leather sets identically; the loose word is "Bracers" in the data, not the picture. (2) "Flat and featureless" does not survive a downscale test. Rendered at true display sizes (15/20/31px plus nearest-neighbour magnification of the actual downscales) alongside the rest of the chitin family: at 15px the glove retains visible finger separation and a better silhouette than chitin_chest, which collapses to an ambiguous vertical smear at the same size. At 20px and 31px the cuff, thumb, outline and highlight all read. It carries the same outline-plus-shading treatment as its set. The "no chitin cue" complaint is inconsistent — no piece in the family (helm, chest, legs, boots) reads as insect plating; all are the same glossy brown leather, which is the set's art direction. The first pass's own description identified the object correctly at a glance, which is itself evidence of recognisability. Icon is legible, family-consistent, and depicts the right slot item. No reroll warranted.

confirms.depicts: A dark blue-grey steel heater shield seen face on, riveted rim and a raised cross down the face. Cleanly drawn and instantly readable as a shield, but entirely achromatic-cool with no warm tone anywhere.
confirms.note: Upheld, though the first pass named the wrong twin. Measured both cuts: painted is 0.00% warm pixels, max saturation 27, mean RGB [58,63,70]; emblem is 0.00% warm, mean [97,107,119]. Both are blue-shifted (B > R), so it is not merely "not ember" but actively cool. The prompt asked for "ash grey iron with embers along the rim" and the ember clause was dropped wholesale — the standard Turbo qualifier-loss failure. That the pipeline can deliver this is proven inside the same batch: moltensteel_shield measures 49.98% warm pixels, mean [84,32,7], and reads as molten even at 16px. Correction to the first pass: the damaging collision is with Iron Shield, not Barrow Shield. Both Cinderguard and Iron Shield are dark blue-grey heater shields with a raised cross; rendered side by side at 31px and 16px they are effectively the same picture. Barrow Shield carries a starburst sigil and is actually a bit more separable. So this is not "merely plain" — the sole discriminator between Cinderguard and a plain metal-tier shield is missing, and in a satchel grid a player would read this as Iron Shield. Severity is weak rather than wrong-object because the object class is right and the silhouette is crisp; it fails on identity, not legibility. Fix direction: drop "shield" (it is pulling the generic heater-shield prior) and name the heat first, e.g. a war shield of blackened scorched iron, its outer edge a band of glowing orange coals with grey ash crusted over the centre.

confirms.depicts: A tall bronze heater shield — pointed at the bottom, curved shoulders — with a raised gold disc boss at its centre. Not a buckler. Both the __painted and __emblem variants show the same heater silhouette.
confirms.note: Upholding the first pass, and the evidence is documentary rather than aesthetic. The game's own item copy at cindervale.html:26691 reads "A light ROUND off-hand for dagger fighters. No block, but +crit, +dodge and +attack speed... Where a shield would only weigh a rogue down." The icon draws the exact thing the description says it is not. The superseded vector art `_bucklerSVG` (cindervale.html:10649) was a pure circle — concentric rings, domed centre boss, four rivets at the corners — so the generated PNG is a regression of a distinction the game previously drew on purpose. The prompt is the cause: "A single shield seen face on, raised boss at its centre, a small round buckler..." leads with the noun "shield", and per the known Turbo failure mode the strongest noun wins while "small round buckler" is discarded as a qualifier. It is the Bronze Shield prompt with words appended. The collision claim also holds and matters mechanically. bronze_shield (line 8714) and bronze_buckler are both ctier 1, both cslot:'shield', crafted at Crafting 9 and 5 respectively, so they co-exist in the satchel and compete for one slot — while being opposite builds (block tank vs no-block crit rogue). I rendered both downscaled to 20px and 16px and magnified: at 20px the only difference is a faint cross on the shield versus a round blob on the buckler, and at 16px they are the same picture. Not merely plain — the icon fails to depict the named item and reads as the sibling item beside it. Suggested reprompt, avoiding the poisoned noun entirely: "A single small round metal disc seen face on, a domed knob at its centre, four rivets spaced near the rim, the whole outline one perfect circle with no point at the bottom, warm brown gold bronze". Same treatment applies to the other nine bucklers (iron_buckler is likewise a heater shield) — this is a family-wide fault, not a one-off.

confirms.depicts: A single hanging cloak with heavy vertical folds and a small silver shoulder clasp — correct object, but the cloth is deep crimson/maroon, not steel.
confirms.note: Not a judgement call — the colour miss is measurable. The shipped variant is picks.json's "painted"; its body samples at mean RGB 87,29,32 (saturated dark red). Every other steel piece renders neutral grey (steel_chest 161,163,165; steel_helm 130,131,132; steel_shield 95,101,112), and every sibling cape carries its own named material's colour correctly (mithril 14,138,223 blue, bronze 112,63,7, runite green, starsteel violet-white). So the cape family genuinely encodes tier by colour and this tile is the one that breaks it — at 15-20px in the satchel it reads as a red cloth cape, closest to warband_cape, not as the steel-tier entry between iron and mithril. Silhouette, folds and clasp are all good, so it stays readable as A cape: weak, not wrong-object. Cause: the prompt ends "...heavy folds, clasp at the top, bright silver steel" and at cfg 2.4 the trailing low-saturation material tag loses to the model's cloak prior, which defaults to red fabric — the vivid-colour siblings (blue/green/violet) survived because their tags fight the prior harder. Fix by stating the material positively and up front rather than as a trailing tag, e.g. "A single hanging cloak of pale grey white metal, the whole cloth cold bare metal from the clasp to the hem, heavy folds, small clasp at the top" — keep "cloak", drop nothing else, and do not add "plate" or "armour" (steel_chest's prompt shows those nouns pull toward a breastplate). The existing emblem variant is a black silhouette and is not a silver substitute; a re-roll is the right remedy.

confirms.depicts: A pointed heater shield seen face-on with a bright crimson-red face, a polished steel rim and a round steel boss at the centre — a red shield, not a steel one.
confirms.note: Confirmed, but not for the reason the first pass led with. The heater silhouette is NOT the defect: I checked all ten bucklers in the ladder (bronze/iron/steel/mithril/cobalt/runite/dawnsteel/moltensteel/starsteel/voidsteel) and every one is the same pointed heater with a central boss, palette-swapped per tier. Shape is a family-wide convention, so changing it here alone would break the set. The colour IS the defect. In this ladder colour is the only tier signal, and steel is the one tier named after an actual grey metal yet it is the only one painted a saturated non-metal hue. Every other steel-tier piece in cut/ is bright silver — steel_shield, steel_chest, steel_helm all check out — so in the gear panel a player sees a silver Steel Shield sitting next to a crimson Steel Buckler in the same tier. At 18px in the satchel its nearest neighbour is moltensteel's orange-red, so it reads as a hotter/higher tier, not tier 3. This is the known red-shield prior beating the prompt: the prompt did say "bright silver steel" and Turbo ignored it. Verified it ships this way — I extracted the live base64 for "steel_buckler" out of cindervale.html and it is the red image, and picks.json still selects "painted". Fix is already sitting on disk and just needs wiring: C:/code/embervale/_iconart/recol_cut/steel_buckler__painted.png is the same silhouette correctly recoloured to silver-grey and matches the rest of the steel tier. Prefer injecting that over a regen. If it is regenerated instead, drop the word "shield" (it drags in the red heater prior) and describe the metal as the object rather than as a qualifier, e.g. "A single round disc of polished pale grey steel seen face on, a domed rivet at its centre, plain unpainted bare metal across the whole face".

confirms.depicts: A scythe: a broad near-white curved crescent blade sweeping to the right off the top of a long diagonal grey haft that runs down to the lower left, with a small dark counterweight nub at the blade's heel.
confirms.note: First pass over-flagged, and two of its three factual claims do not hold. Name is "Bone Reaper", prompt "A single scythe, one long curved pale bone blade on a dark haft" — the icon on sheet 5 (the __emblem__ variant, verified by cropping audit-05.png row 0 col 2) is exactly that. Measured on the 128px source: ink bbox is 104x116, i.e. 81% of frame width and 91% of height, so the frame is not "near-empty"; the object is centred and fills it. Luminance p50 is 215 against a dark card, so value contrast is strong, not faint. Downscaled with a box filter to 31, 20 and 15px and viewed pixel-magnified: at all three the crescent-plus-diagonal-haft silhouette survives intact and reads as a scythe, not a "diagonal scratch" — 49 of 225 pixels carry the form at 15px, 35 of them at over 55% alpha. The one fair part of the critique is that the haft renders mid-grey rather than the dark the prompt asked for, so blade-vs-haft separation is modest at 15px, and the pale blade could be read as steel as easily as bone. That is a nuance of material, not of object identity — a player sees a scythe, which is what a Bone Reaper is. Note also that a __painted__ variant exists (dark red haft, much stronger haft/blade contrast) and would be the better pick if a future pass wants to strengthen this one, but the shipped emblem is not a defect. Files: C:/code/embervale/_iconart/cut/bone_reaper__emblem.png and C:/code/embervale/_iconart/cut/bone_reaper__painted.png.

confirms.depicts: A black square tile carrying a violet-outlined standing human figure — round glowing orb head, torso, two arms angled out, two legs. A person on a plaque, not cloth.
confirms.note: Live variant is __emblem (picks.json: "voidweave": "emblem"), and it is the humanoid the first pass described. At 15-20px the figure's head-plus-limbs silhouette is the only shape that survives, so a player reads it as a spirit/ghost item, never as folded fabric. Not a judgement call. Cheapest fix: the unpicked voidweave__painted.png in the same folder is already close to right — a dark folded mass with violet light in the interior creases, bold silhouette, good value contrast — so flipping the pick to "painted" resolves this without a regen. If regenerating instead, drop "rift" (it is doing the spectral-apparition work alongside the item name) and give the fold a concrete shape: "A single square of near black cloth folded flat into a thick stack, the top corner turned back so a thin violet glow shows deep between the layers. Just the folded fabric lying by itself — no head, no limbs, no standing shape, no person."

confirms.depicts: A malformed pale-grey glove with fingers at BOTH ends — four fingers and a thumb splayed at the top, and a second row of five stubby rounded finger lobes along the bottom edge, separated by the same ink lines as the real fingers. No wrist opening and no cuff anywhere. The picked variant is "painted" (picks.json); the unused "emblem" variant is a clean, correctly-formed glove with a wide cuff band.
confirms.note: The first pass's stated reason is the weaker half of the case — "it's a glove, not a bracer" would not on its own be worth flagging, since hand-slot gear is routinely drawn as a glove and the prompt itself asked for one ("A single soft leather glove, fingers curled, wide cuff at the wrist"). The real problem is that Turbo produced a doubled hand. Verified by cropping the lower third at 6x: the bottom edge is a second set of five finger lobes with finger-separation lines, not a cuff or fringe. The prompt's "wide cuff at the wrist" was dropped entirely — the model closed the wrist end with more fingers instead. Consequence at display size: downscaled to 16px it is a symmetric grey lump with notches on all sides and no identifiable silhouette; at 31px it reads as a paw, a shell, or a crown before it reads as hand armour. Its four siblings (ogre_boots / helm / legs / chest) are clean and instantly readable at the same size, and ogre_legs already establishes that this set draws limb armour as a PAIR, which is also the natural silhouette for bracers. Two independent fixes available: (a) zero-cost — flip picks.json for ogre_gloves from "painted" to "emblem"; the existing emblem cut is a correct single glove with a cuff, though still a glove rather than a bracer; (b) reroll toward the item's actual name and the set's paired look. Suggested subject sentence, no "glove" noun (it carries the five-finger prior that caused the doubling) and stating the open ends positively: "Two matching thick pale grey hide forearm cuffs standing side by side, each a wide tube of stitched hide with a laced seam down the front, open and empty at the top and bottom — just the two cuffs, no hands, no fingers, no arms."

confirms.depicts: A vertical mithril-blue hammer: a flared, faceted block head with a flat top and angled shoulders sitting at the top of a slim shaft, with a small round pommel at the base.
confirms.note: First pass overcalled. Its core claim - "no hammer head, nothing protrudes sideways" - is measurably false. From the alpha channel of the 128px source the head is 44px against an 18px shaft, a 2.44x flare, byte-identical to steel_hammer (44/18) and in line with iron (2.67) and bronze (2.58). It is a blocky faceted trapezoid, not a knob or ball, so it does not read as a pin or lollipop. At 15px it renders as a distinct light-blue block on a stem, not a line with a dot. Fair partial point: the head flares slightly wider at the top and the handle is long and slim rather than the "huge square head, short thick handle" the prompt asked for, making this the plainest of the blue hammers (cobalt_hammer, at 3.00x with a clear T-crossbar, is much stronger at 15px). But plain is not wrong: in a gear slot labelled Mithril Hammer, mass concentrated in a block atop a shaft is unambiguously the hammer/maul class, and flagging mithril while steel and iron use identical construction would be inconsistent. Only worth revisiting as part of a family-wide pass to fatten every hammer head toward cobalt's proportions.

confirms.depicts: An orange flame with three licking tongues rising out of a dark red circular dish or brazier rim. A fire, not a material.
confirms.note: First pass is right. Item is "Ember Dust", prompt was "A small conical heap of glowing ember orange dust, hot sparks rising from it" - the noun "ember" beat "dust" and Turbo drew a bonfire. picks.json selects "painted", which is the flame; there is no heap, no granular texture, no cone. Two aggravating factors beyond it merely being plain: (1) ash__painted.png, the item sitting right beside it in the satchel as the other firemaking residue, IS a clean grey conical heap - so the correct silhouette exists in the same family and Ember Dust is the odd one out; (2) shade_ember__painted.png is the identical flame drawing in violet, so at 15-20px these two unrelated items (firemaking byproduct vs rare monster drop) are the same icon in two hues. A player reads this as the firemaking skill / a bonfire, not as the residue they stockpile 120 at a time for tools. Cheap fix available: ember_dust__emblem.png already reads as an orange conical mound with a small flame on top, so flipping the pick from "painted" to "emblem" may be enough. If re-prompting, avoid the words ember and fire entirely and state the absence positively - e.g. "A small low cone of coarse orange red powder heaped on the ground, grey crusted on the outside, a few points glowing deep inside it. Just the loose powder itself, settled and still."

confirms.depicts: A sledgehammer: a bevelled square head overhanging a straight dark haft with a rounded pommel, black iron cracked with orange glow.
confirms.note: First pass's reason is measurably false. Head spans 38px (x45-82) over a 16px shaft (x56-71) — an 11px overhang each side, ratio 2.38, mid-pack for the hammer family (iron 2.57, steel 2.44, mithril 2.44, starsteel 1.96, voidsteel 1.87). Checked at 4x and at a true 16px downscale: it reads as a blocky maul, the same silhouette all eleven tier hammers share, and the emblem cut adds notched shoulders on the head. Fair nitpicks that don't make it wrong: the head is near-square (38x34) rather than a wide striking bar, and the near-black haft under a bright head is low-contrast on a dark panel — both traits shared with unflagged tiers. A torch reads as a flame plume; this is a geometric block with a pommel below it. No prompt change needed.

confirms.depicts: Two rolled bundles of brown leather standing on end side by side, lashed together with a cord tied in a knot around the middle; the open spiral ends of both rolls are visible as flat rims at the top.
confirms.note: Inspected the picked variant (picks.json says painted) at 512px and re-rendered at 15/20/31px. This is not a sack. The silhouette is widest at the TOP and flares outward, the cord sits at the mid-body rather than at a neck, and there is no gathered drawstring or buckled flap — both cylinders show open flat rolled rims. That is the standard genre icon for tanned leather stock, and it is exactly what the prompt asked for ("a single rolled bundle of plain tanned leather tied with cord, standing on end"). It is also deliberately distinct from the raw-material pelts in the same library (ratskin/Raw Hide, wolf_pelt, boar_hide etc. all use the flat stretched-skin template seen from above), so the processed vs raw distinction reads correctly in the grid. The first pass's asks — "no skin outline, no folded flaps" — would actually make it a duplicate of the raw pelt template and lose that distinction. At 15px it is a brown mass with a lighter horizontal band, but so is every small item at 15px; at 20px the two lobes and the tie are legible and at 31px the rolls are unmistakable. Nearby pouch-type icons are not confusable: the seed pouches are coloured cloth cinched at the neck with a seed at the mouth, and Forager's Pouch is a small belt pouch with a buckled flap. Merely plain and monochrome brown, not wrong.

confirms.depicts: A single centred teardrop of warm translucent orange-gold amber with a glossy specular highlight on the upper left; the painted variant deepens to red-brown at the base, the emblem variant is lighter and more golden.
confirms.note: First pass was mistaken. A warm orange-gold teardrop is the standard shorthand for amber — amber IS fossilised tree resin, and resin drops are teardrop-shaped, so this is the correct reference class rather than a substituted one. The prompt asked for "a single teardrop of deep amber resin, warm translucent orange gold" and that is precisely what rendered; no wrong-noun prior took over. Checked for in-set collision too, since "generic orange drop" only bites if a sibling looks the same: every other teardrop in audit-manifest.json is a gem pendant on a gold chain (amethyst, ruby, sapphire, dragonstone, void gem), all carrying a chain silhouette above the stone. deep_amber is the only free-standing droplet in the library, which makes it more distinguishable in the satchel grid, not less. Silhouette is bold and value contrast is strong, so it survives 15px. Only real shortfall: the "trapped spark inside" never rendered, and the hot specular reads faintly wet rather than solid — a fidelity nitpick against the prompt, not a failure of identification. Not worth a reprompt; the noun is working.

confirms.depicts: A single upright bright silver blade filling the frame: a faceted point at the top, a thin bar with rounded ends laid across the middle, and the same silver metal continuing below the bar and tapering to a second point at the bottom. No wrapped grip and no pommel.
confirms.note: The first pass saw it accurately at full size — the blade really does continue past the crossbar to a second point, so there is no handle, and the prompt asked for the opposite ("small round pommel, no crossguard"). But it over-weights it. At 15px and 20px, the sizes this is actually shown at, the missing grip is invisible; the icon reads as a bright vertical blade with a crossguard, which is a dagger. The "vanishes at 15px" part is wrong — it is one of the brighter icons in the dagger row (light silver on dark); iron_dagger is the dim one. Most decisively, the no-grip/second-point structure is the family convention in this batch: bronze_dagger and runite_dagger taper to a point below the guard in exactly the same way and were not flagged, so regenerating steel alone would make it the outlier. The real residual issue, if a batch pass ever happens, is that at 20px steel_dagger and steel_sword are near-identical silhouettes separated only by thickness — and the sword is the one that got a proper wrapped grip and pommel. A family-wide fix would be to state the handle positively in the prompt ("the lower third is a plain wrapped handle ending in a round knob, not a blade") rather than to re-roll this one icon.

confirms.depicts: A heater shield seen face on, filled solid black, with a thick white inner rim and a black outer stroke. No boss, bevel, rivets or material texture. The emblem variant is identical plus a warm orange glow along the top edge.
confirms.note: Not a miss. The item IS a shield (cslot:'shield', T9, def 78) and the icon is unambiguously a shield — the silhouette is the cleanest in the whole shield family and it holds up better than most at 18px because the value contrast is absolute. The flavour text is literally "A shield of solid absence. Blows land on it and simply stop being," so a featureless void-black face is on-theme rather than a failure; the prompt asked for "black disc inside a thick bright white rim" and got exactly that. The first pass's read of the pixels was correct, its verdict was not: this is plain, not wrong, and the skeptic bar (player would not recognise it, or would name it as something else) is not met. Worth flagging for Jordan as a style note, not a defect: the white rim is a hard outline stroke rather than a lit edge, which is a language outlier next to painted siblings like voidsteel_shield (rivets, cross fuller, rendered metal) and moltensteel_shield, and it does carry a faint security-badge association. If he ever wants it warmer, the family already solves "black shield" with an edge treatment — a prompt closer to "a single shield seen face on, seamless void black face with no boss and no rivets, a thin cold white halo burning along its outer edge" would keep the absence theme while giving it a material read. Low priority; do not regenerate on this report alone.

confirms.depicts: A dark trapezoidal metal ingot at a three-quarter angle whose top face is a hot orange-gold glow fading to red, with only a thin violet-magenta wash on the lower body and base seams.
confirms.note: First pass is right. Object class is correct (unmistakably a cast ingot), but the material read is wrong: 45% orange / 28% red / 16% magenta and only 8% violet in the lit pixels, versus 58-97% violet across the rest of the voidsteel family (voidsteel_helm__painted is 97% violet). At 18px the violet vanishes and it reads as a dark bar with a fire-lit top face - i.e. near-identical to molten_bar, an actual item in the same game (78% red / 20% orange, also a dark bar with a glowing channel). Since all bars share one silhouette, colour IS the tier identifier, so this is a real mis-ID against molten/bronze, not just a plain icon. No regeneration needed - this is a variant-selection bug. picks.json sets "voidsteel_bar": "emblem", and it is the ONLY one of the 12 bars not set to "painted". voidsteel_bar__painted.png already exists, is 94.5% violet, matches the prompt ("near black metal with violet rift light in the seams") and matches the family. Fix: change picks.json to "voidsteel_bar": "painted". Prompt itself is fine and should not be rewritten.

confirms.depicts: A saturated orange-yellow gold ingot lying flat at a three-quarter angle, dark gold outline, cream-yellow top face. No white-hot metal, no glow, no sparks. Pixel-for-pixel the same reference class, palette, pose and top-face highlight as the existing gold_bar icon.
confirms.note: Confirmed, but as a collision rather than a wrong subject. The ingot form came out exactly as prompted, so the object class is right; what failed is the material, which in this family IS the identity. Every other bar is separated purely by palette (silver = white-grey, starsteel = lilac, molten = dark brown with an orange core), so a bar rendered in gold's exact hue is indistinguishable from Gold Bar, a different item that appears in the same satchel grid. A player would name it Gold Bar. Cause: the prompt reads "molten white gold metal wreathed in faint falling sparks" — the noun "gold" carried the prior and the model answered it with a stock gold ingot, discarding "molten", "white" and the sparks, the same way "ogre" beat "hide". A rewrite must not contain the word gold anywhere. Describe the material by its own appearance instead: a bar of blinding white metal, near-white at the centre fading to pale blue-grey at the corners, with a few bright pinpoint specks lifting off the top face. Keep the long tapered ingot shape sentence, which worked, and drop the sparks if they cost value contrast, since the white body alone separates it from every other bar at 15px.

confirms.depicts: A single whole grilled fish, side on, head left, golden-brown crisp skin with dark char bands; the painted variant carries a distinctly slate-grey/olive dorsal band over the gold, the emblem variant is plainer gold with a pale head.
confirms.note: Not confirmed. The icon depicts exactly what its prompt asked for and what the item is: a cooked fish. Cooked Shark is food, not a live animal, so the absence of a dorsal fin and snout is correct behaviour, not a miss — raw_shark__painted is an unmistakable shark, so the family already carries the shark cue where it belongs. Two of the first pass's specifics are wrong on inspection: there IS a differentiating cue (a slate-grey/olive dorsal band, matching the prompt's "slate grey and brown", and it is the only cooked fish in the set carrying grey), and the silhouettes are not pixel-for-pixel identical — shark, sardine, swordfish, tuna, salmon and minnow are six separate generations at different rotations. What is true is that all six read as "small golden cooked fish" at 20px, but that is a deliberate family-wide style decision baked into every prompt ("A single cooked fish, side on, head to the left, golden brown grilled skin with dark char marks…"), not a defect in this one icon — flagging cooked_shark alone would be arbitrary. Genuine weakness, worth noting but below the confirm bar: nothing conveys "large", and the whole-fish framing is odd for shark, which is eaten as steak. If the family is ever differentiated as a batch, the lever for this one is size and cut, not fins — e.g. "A single thick round grilled steak of pale fish, one dark spine bone in the centre, seared brown grill bars across the top" — but that breaks the family silhouette and should be a deliberate whole-set decision.

confirms.depicts: A single coiled serpentine eel seen side-on, blunt head at the upper left with a visible eye and a small pectoral fin, body curling down into a closed C-loop tail. Bright ember-orange lighting across the head and upper back, body falling to near-black with a faint violet rim along the underside of the loop.
confirms.note: Live pick for this id is the EMBLEM variant (confirmed in _iconart/picks.json: raw_voideel -> emblem), which is what the first pass saw. I resampled it to a true 15/21/31px render composited over the real satchel tile colour (#1a1209, from .inv-ic in cindervale.html) and measured it. Both first-pass claims are overstated. (1) Readability: the head and upper back peak at 8.79:1 contrast against the tile — the icon does not vanish, it reads at 15px as a bright warm head with a dark curled body, and the coil keeps a violet rim that holds the outline at 21px and up. The lower loop is admittedly dim (79% of body pixels sit within 1.5:1 of the tile), so it loses some definition, but the silhouette and the "coiled eel" reading survive. (2) Colour: yes, the dominant accent is ember orange rather than violet, but violet is present along the belly, and every other fish in this family is lit the same warm way — a player reads "eel", not "wrong item". Name flavour vs. lighting is a style nit, not a depiction failure. It is also clearly distinct from cooked_voideel, which is a straight fish silhouette with a forked tail. Worth flagging separately for Jordan: the PAINTED variant of this same id is a genuine failure — max luminance 34 vs tile 19, 1.22:1 contrast, 100% of body pixels invisible against the tile. It is an unreadable black blob. If the pick ever flips from emblem to painted, this icon dies. The emblem pick is the right call and should stay.

confirms.depicts: A single curved amber-orange plate with a heavy dark red-brown rim and a curled, tapering left edge — a hard shell segment seen face-on, plain-surfaced apart from a soft gradient.
confirms.note: Live pick is the emblem (picks.json: chitin => emblem), and that is the one the first pass saw. Downsampled it myself to 16/20/31px on the dark UI ground: the first pass's core complaint is wrong on the facts — saturated amber against near-black is one of the highest-contrast icons in the set, and the silhouette (tapered plate, curled left edge, thick dark rim) survives 16px cleanly. It is not depicting another object and it is not a blob. It IS plain — no segmentation, ridging or specular hit — so the criticism that it lacks shell character is fair, but plain is not the bar for a flag; item is "Chitin Plating" and what is drawn is a curved amber plate. Nothing else live collides with it either: tanned_hide is a rolled bundle, ogre_hide a stretched pelt, chitin_shard a spiky fragment. Important for anyone tempted to "fix" this by swapping variants: chitin__painted is the documented armour-noun failure — a full chibi suit of plate armour — so the emblem pick is already the escape hatch and must stay. If it is ever regenerated for polish, the gain is surface detail only (overlapping segment ridges, one hard gloss streak); the prompt should drop the word "armour" entirely, e.g. "A single curved amber shell segment with three overlapping ridged bands across it and a glossy highlight, thick at the top edge and tapering to a thin lip".

confirms.depicts: A plump golden-orange grilled fish seen side-on, tilted head-up-left, with four dark char bars across the flank and a fan tail. Blunt rounded snout, no bill of any kind.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is not just "plain" — I checked it against its own family. Picked variant is __painted (per picks.json). Rendered the six cooked fish plus raw_swordfish at 128px and at 16px on a dark ground: cooked_sardine, cooked_trout, cooked_tuna and cooked_swordfish are the same picture — same orange-gold body, same dark char bars, same fan tail — separable only by body tilt, which is gone by 20px. cooked_shark is the one that survives, because it is grey-green rather than orange. So the swordfish does not read as a different object, but a player picking food out of the satchel would take it for cooked trout or cooked tuna. The prompt did ask for "long flat bill" and the model dropped it, so this is a prompt-adherence miss, not a design choice. It is also inconsistent with its own raw partner: raw_swordfish__painted has a long spike bill and sickle fins and is instantly a swordfish even at 16px, so the raw/cooked pair does not read as the same species. The emblem variant is no better — same billless body, plus a detached blob floating above it. Fix direction: lead the sentence with the bill as the object's defining shape rather than listing it last, and give the body a silhouette the other cooked fish do not have, e.g. "A long spear nosed fish lying side on, a straight pointed bill running out the full left side of the frame as long as its head, tall crescent back fin, cooked golden brown skin with dark char bars, deep steak thick body." Keep the bill horizontal and frame-spanning so it survives the downscale, and steer the body colour off the shared orange (deeper browned crust) so it stops matching trout and tuna.

confirms.depicts: An erupting volcano — a dark brown cone with bright orange-red lava streaks pouring down the near face and grey-white smoke/ash clouds billowing around its base.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and worse than the first pass described. Live pick in picks.json is "painted", which is the volcano. Viewed at 4x the red is not a maroon tint, it is lava: two saturated orange-red flows running from the summit down the slope, plus rolling grey smoke clouds at the base rather than rubble. The prompt's "conical heap ... faint pale wisps" handed Turbo a cone plus wisps, and it answered with its volcano prior; the word "dust" contributed nothing. At 18px and 31px it is a red cone on a pale grey pad — reads as a volcano or a traffic cone, never as fine grey grave dust, and it is also the only red item in a barrow set that is otherwise dark slate/bone. Fix direction: drop the cone silhouette and the word "dust" as the lead noun. Something like "A low flat-topped pile of pale grey powdered ash, wide and shallow, its top surface smooth and its edges crumbling into loose grains, a few coarse bone-white specks scattered across it. Just the loose powder itself — no mountain, no smoke, no fire, no container."

confirms.depicts: Two nested crescent moons — a large lower-right crescent with a smaller crescent tucked inside its upper-left — both solid flat black with only a thin orange rim light. It reads as a moon-phase emblem, not a claw.
confirms.note:
Upheld, and worse than "weak". picks.json selects the __emblem variant for this item, and at 4x that variant is unambiguously TWO crescents arranged as a moon motif, not one claw. Every defining claw cue is missing: no broad root or knuckle, no taper from thick base to single point, both ends of each crescent come to equal sharp tips, and there is no keratin ridging or internal value break. The duplication is the killer — a second crescent nested inside the first is a moon-phase symbol and reads as nothing else. At 31px it is clearly a moon; at 16px on the dark satchel ground the near-black fill vanishes into the panel and only the orange rim survives, so it collapses to a dark ring/O. A player would call this "moon", not "Alpha Claw".

The __painted variant is not a rescue — it is an amorphous black S/3 shape of two commas, even less claw-like.

Root cause is the prompt: "A single large black curved claw, hooked and worn" gives Turbo no shape to build, and "curved + black + hooked" lands straight on its crescent prior. Two fixes are needed together — describe the silhouette concretely, and make it not-black so it survives on a dark panel. Suggested subject sentence:

A single thick wolf talon standing upright, wide and heavy where it was torn from the paw at the bottom, swelling into one blunt knuckle and then narrowing along a smooth outward curve to one sharp point at the top, the outer edge banded with pale growth ridges, bone-grey at the root darkening to charcoal at the tip. Just the one detached talon — no paw, no toes, no second claw, no animal.

Key changes: "talon" instead of "claw" to move off the crescent prior, an explicit wide root vs single point so the taper is asymmetric, "Just the one" stated positively to kill the duplication, and a grey-to-charcoal value ramp so there is internal contrast instead of a flat black hole.

confirms.depicts: A smooth glossy solid green cone with a hard black outline, wet specular highlights down its face, and a clean unbroken curved base — reads as a blob of green jelly, a slime, or a small hill. A 3-4px pale wisp floats at the upper right, invisible below ~32px.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is a material failure rather than mere plainness. The surface is sealed and glossy with specular highlights, which actively says wet solid — the opposite of powder — and the base is a single continuous curve with no spill, no grain, no loose edge anywhere. Nothing in the image is granular. The decisive check is barrow_dust__painted.png, built from the near-identical sibling prompt ("A small conical heap of fine grey barrow dust, faint pale wisps"): that one has scattered loose granules spilling out along the bottom and reads immediately as a pile of powder. Set side by side, cursed_dust is plainly not the same class of object. Worse, at satchel size the glossy green dome collides with ectoplasm__painted.png (translucent green blob) — a player scanning the grid would read this as slime, not dust. Prompt lever: "cursed dust" gave the generator nothing to draw, so it answered "conical heap" with a smooth mound prior. Describe the spill instead of the heap — a low scattered drift of coarse ashen grey-green grains, wider than it is tall, its edges breaking into loose scattered specks on the ground, dull and powdery with no shine. Drop the word cone entirely, drop the wisp (it cannot survive 15px), and shift the hue toward ash grey so it stops reading as jelly.

confirms.depicts: A matching pair of pale-grey leg guards standing upright side by side, front-on and symmetric, running from a rounded knee cap down over a soft bulging shin to a small rounded toe cap, with a seam across each shin and one small stud per leg. Soft broad gradient shading, dark-grey (not black) outline, rounded lumpy contours.
confirms.note: First pass over-flagged; its three specific claims do not survive checking the file at 3x against its neighbours. (1) "Hard highlights and rivets" is wrong — the shading is soft broad gradients with a single small stud per leg; iron_legs is the one with the black outline, faceted planes and bright specular streaks. (2) "Same silhouette as the metal-tier legs" is factually false — iron/steel/mithril legs are 3/4-view with pronounced sabatons and overlapping articulated knee plates, while ogre_legs is a flat front-on symmetric pair with rounded contours. (3) "No hide look" ignores that its surface treatment is a near-exact match for ogre_boots__painted.png (unflagged) and that the entire Ogrehide set is pale grey by design — ogre_chest sits at the same value. The prompt asked for "thick pale grey hide" and the set colour identity is consistent across chest/boots/legs. At 15-20px it reads as a pair of pale-grey leg armour: correct slot, correct set colour, and lighter and footless enough to separate from iron's darker sabatoned pair, with the tooltip name carrying the rest. The material sits between stiff padded hide and plate rather than landing squarely on plate — a judgement call on texture, which is the "merely plain rather than wrong" case. One residual nitpick not worth a re-roll: the shape is shin-guard-shaped rather than thigh-covering as "Chaps" implies, but the prompt specified shin guards, so that is a prompt-authoring choice rather than a generation failure. Verified by rendering ogre_legs vs iron_legs vs ogre_boots at 3x and a 15/20/31px strip against bronze/iron/steel/mithril legs.

confirms.depicts: A tall faceted crystal, body near-black with clearly violet interior facets down the left and lower half, and a small warm white-to-amber specular highlight on the top facet.
confirms.note: First pass over-read the tip highlight. The warm area is only the top ~15% of the shape; the body is near-black with visible violet facets, exactly what the prompt asked for ("near black with violet light trapped inside"). Rendered at 18px and 31px on the dark satchel ground it reads as the darkest icon in its row — a dark crystal with a lit tip, not an ember gem. A fire gem reads saturated orange throughout: dragon_gem__emblem is solid orange edge to edge and ruby__emblem solid red, and neither is confusable with this at small size. The warm cap is also the void family's shared specular treatment, not a rogue flame — cut_void__emblem and void_shard__emblem carry the identical warm highlight on their top light-facing facet, so singling this one out is inconsistent. No competing item it could be mistaken for either: void_cinder is a keyhole silhouette with a purple orb, emberbloom is a flower. The missing "rocky matrix" from the prompt is shared by amethyst, ruby and sapphire, so it is a family convention rather than a defect here. The objection is colour-language (void light ought to be violet), not a recognition failure. FYI only, not a recommendation: void_crystal__painted.png is a uniform deep violet with no warm cap and would be a drop-in swap if the family highlight is ever revisited, but it is flatter and lower-contrast at 18px, which is presumably why the emblem was picked.

confirms.depicts: A small fire: three upward-licking tongues glowing bright orange-yellow at the top, fading down a fire gradient into a near-black tapered point at the base. Reads as a flame / ember flare, not a piece of shell.
confirms.note: Live variant is the emblem (picks.json: "chitin_shard": "emblem"), which is what the first pass saw. Confirmed and I'd rate it harder than "weak": rendered at 16/20/31px against the satchel ground, the three top tongues plus the bright-top/black-bottom ramp make it a textbook flame silhouette. In a game that already has firemaking, Ember Dust and ember-named items, a player would file this as a fire item, not "Chitin Shard". The palette clash the first pass mentioned is real too — Chitin Plating is a bright golden-amber curved plate, so the two never read as the same material. Note the alternate is no rescue: chitin_shard__painted is a rounded dark-maroon cube that reads as a gem or a block of something, not a jagged splinter, and it is also off-palette from the plating. This needs a re-render, not a variant swap. The prompt "A single jagged splinter of glossy dark chitin" is too thin for Turbo — "jagged" plus "dark" with no shape detail let the flame prior win. Suggested subject sentence, shape-first and matching the plating's amber so the family reads: "A single broken sliver of hard golden amber shell, long and narrow, one straight snapped edge down the left side and a torn ragged edge down the right, coming to a sharp point at the top, thick and solid with a wet glossy sheen. Just the broken piece of shell — no fire, no glow, no creature."

confirms.depicts: A single dark crimson leather glove, palm toward the viewer, four separated fingers and a thumb, with a darker riveted cuff band across the wrist.
confirms.note: First pass is factually off on both counts. The fingers are individually separated with gaps that survive downscaling — I rendered it at 15px, 20px and 31px against three satchel background values and the hand silhouette holds on all of them; it is more legible than ogre_gloves or void_gloves in the same row. There is also cuff detail: a darker band with a rivet line at the wrist, still readable at 15px. The glove-vs-bracer point is a family-wide convention, not a defect in this icon: all nine leather hand items (ogre_gloves, wolf_gloves, demon_gloves, void_gloves, rough_gloves, troll_gloves, chitin_gloves, ember_gloves, wraith_gloves) are named "-hide Bracers" and every one is prompted with the identical "A single soft leather glove, fingers curled, wide cuff at the wrist" string; the item id is drake_gloves, a hands slot. Only real weakness is that dark crimson sits closer to the dark panel ground than the brighter siblings do, but it is not close to unreadable. A player sees a red leather glove and identifies the hand-slot piece correctly.

confirms.depicts: A single grey sleeveless vest seen front-on, filling the frame — V-neck opening, darker charcoal shoulder band, three small buttons down the front placket, empty with no head, body or sleeves. The emblem variant is the same vest silhouette in flat line art with no buttons at all.
confirms.note: Over-flagged. The item is "Grave-Shroud Vest" and the icon is unambiguously a grey sleeveless vest — correct object, correct colour family, bold readable silhouette, hollow and empty as the prompt asked. The buttons and lapel seam the first pass objected to are ~2px of dark pixel at the 15-20px satchel size and vanish entirely; the emblem cut has no buttons whatsoever, so half the stated reason applies to neither variant a player sees at scale. The real shortfall is flavour: it is not tattered, frayed or grave-stained, so it reads as generic cloth armour rather than rotted burial linen. That is plain, not wrong — a player recognises it as the torso gear it is and would not call it something else. If regenerated for flavour later, fix it at shape level (ragged uneven torn hem with hanging strips, no fasteners) rather than with adjectives like "rotted", which Turbo drops at cfg 2.4.

confirms.depicts: A green two-pointed leaf or sprout: a V-notch splits the top into two separate tips, the bottom is a flat straight-cut edge like a pot rim, and a dark curl sits in the middle. Reads as a leaf pair or a small green flame, not an ear.
confirms.note: Verified independently at 128px, 31px and 16px (box-downsampled over white). The failure is structural, not a detail loss: an ear is one continuous lobe with ONE tip and a rounded fleshy base, but this silhouette has two tips separated by a deep notch and a truncated flat bottom. That is a leaf/sprout shape. The notch is the largest feature so it is the one thing that DOES survive to 15px, while the inner curl (the only ear-like cue) is the first thing to go. Cindervale already has green foraged herbs in the same satchel grid, so a player would file this under plants. The emblem variant is no better - a rounded green diamond with a faint curl, reading as a gem or leaf. Upgrading the first pass from weak to wrong-object because this is a misidentification, not merely a plain icon. Prompt cause: "A single severed pointed green goblin ear" gives Turbo nothing to draw except "pointed green thing", and its prior for that is foliage; "severed" and "ear" both lose. Suggested rewrite (subject sentence only, no style words): "A single long tapering pointed ear lying flat, one narrow lobe rising to one sharp tip at the top and a rounded fleshy lobe at the bottom, a deep curved hollow bowl carved into the middle of its inner face, a thick rolled rim running down the outer edge, mottled sickly green skin, a dark red cut edge across the bottom where it was cut away. Just the one detached ear - no head, no face, no creature." Note the deliberate omission of the word "goblin", which risks producing a whole goblin, and the explicit "one sharp tip" to kill the two-point notch.

confirms.depicts: A faceted angular shard whose upper two-thirds is a bright orange-to-cream glow with a near-black lower body and a thin violet rim along the bottom-left edge. At satchel size it reads as a burning ember or hot coal, not a void gem.
confirms.note: First pass is right and this is not a judgement call - it is measurable. The shipped variant is the emblem (picks.json has "void_shard": "emblem"). Of the pixels bright enough to survive the downscale (L>0.42, 26% of the shard body) 93% are warm orange/cream and only 7% are violet; the brightest pixel is rgb(254,240,210), hue 41. The prompt asked for "near black with violet light along its broken edges" and the generator gave the opposite value structure - the void colour survives only as a dim edge that vanishes below ~20px. Rendered at 16/20/31px on a dark satchel ground the shard reads as a glowing ember chip. This matters more than usual because the item is in the gems_cut family, where hue IS the identity that separates one cut gem from another, and the game already ships void_cinder, ember_log and shade_ember - warm-orange items it would be confused with. Shape and silhouette are fine; only the palette fails. No regeneration is needed: void_shard__painted.png in the same folder is the same shard with correct near-black/violet values (100% of its bright pixels are violet, brightest rgb(217,173,253) hue 273) and reads unmistakably as a void gem at 16px. Flipping picks.json from "emblem" to "painted" fixes it outright. Only caveat is that the painted variant is darker overall (9% of its body is bright vs 26%), so it is a quieter tile in the grid - still clearly a violet crystal, but worth a glance beside its gems_cut siblings for value consistency.

confirms.depicts: A thick glossy white crescent moon, horns curling toward the upper right, on empty ground. No petals, no bloom, no stem, no leaves, nothing botanical anywhere in the frame.
confirms.note: Verified on the shipped file: picks.json selects "painted" for moonpetal, and C:/code/embervale/_iconart/cut/moonpetal__painted.png is a crescent moon glyph. The classic Turbo failure — prompt was "A single luminous white moon flower with a pale silver glow" and the noun "moon" beat "flower", same as ogre_hide/everflame_rod. Downsampled to 16px the crescent's horns close into a solid white ring, so a player sees a pearl or a plain O-token, not even a moon. Worse in context: Moonpetal is family=herbs, a farmable crop with a matching moonpetal_seed, and every sibling (frostcrocus, ashbloom, witchhazel, emberbloom) renders as a clear petalled flower — this one is the only non-plant in the row. The "petal" half of the name has no representation at all. The emblem variant is not a rescue: it is the same crescent knocked out as a black hole inside an 8-point star badge, which reads worse. Fix by deleting the word "moon" from the prompt entirely rather than qualifying it — e.g. "A single white flower with five broad rounded overlapping petals fanned wide open around a pale silver centre, on one short green stem with two narrow leaves." Keeps the pale silver read that justifies the name without ever handing the model the lunar prior.

confirms.depicts: A glowing molten-orange bone: two flared knobs at the top, two at the bottom, pinched waist — the canonical dog-bone/femur silhouette, tilted. No ridges, spines, horns or plate edges anywhere. The emblem variant is a plain tapered column with slightly flared ends, reading as a pillar rather than a crest.
confirms.note: Confirmed. "Bony" won over "crest plate" — the documented Turbo failure. Ember Crest is the Emberwyrm boss-summon key (sell 18,000), described in game as "the molten brow-crest of an elder drake", so it needs to read as a ridged/horned plate. It reads as a bone. Sheet audit-00 also holds ancient_bone, gnawed_bone and bone_charm, so at 15px this is a fourth bone shape distinguished only by colour, and it will not read as a family with its sibling infernal_crest. Kept at "weak" rather than "wrong-object": the material and ember palette are correct and the orange keeps it findable among the grey bones. Suggested reprompt (drops the noun that carries the bone prior, gives a concrete shape, states the absence positively): "A fan of five tall pointed spines standing in a row along one thick curved base bar, the middle spine tallest and the end ones short, dark charcoal with molten orange cracks glowing in the gaps between the spines, standing upright and filling the frame. Just the fan of spines on its own — no skull, no head, no living animal."

confirms.depicts: A featureless solid-black dome with a flared skirt, outlined in ember orange with a small glowing dot at the apex. The outer contour is a hood contour, but the interior is filled solid, so no face opening, no fabric folds, no hood mouth. At satchel size it reads as a bell, an egg, or a chess pawn rather than a cowl.
confirms.note: Confirmed, but the first pass misdiagnosed the cause and the fix is not a reprompt. Two assets exist for this id. ember_helm__painted.png is an excellent cowl — peaked hood, clear dark face opening, shoulder drape, charred black hide cracked with ember orange, exactly the prompt. The generation succeeded. The sheet is showing ember_helm__emblem.png, and the emblem flattening filled in the face opening, which is the one feature that makes a hood a hood. Proof it is the treatment and not the subject: drake_helm__emblem.png in the same row keeps a distinctly darker face hole inside its hood outline and is instantly readable as a cowl, and every other Emberhide piece on the sheet keeps its own defining negative space (the notch between the boot shafts, the finger splits on the bracers, the V of the jerkin). This is the only one that lost its interior. Fix by using the painted variant for this id, or by making the emblem pass preserve the face opening the way drake_helm's does. Rewriting the prompt would waste a generation on art that is already correct.

confirms.depicts: A single charred-black leather glove, five fingers up, thick orange-lit cuff at the wrist and glowing ember cracks running through the palm. Bold, centred, one object, very high value contrast against the keyed background.
confirms.note:
The first pass is factually right and practically wrong. The item is "Emberhide Bracers" (C:/code/embervale/cindervale.html:26074, `_LSLOT_NOUN={...gloves:'Bracers'...}`) and the prompt in audit-07.json literally asked for "A single soft leather glove, fingers curled, wide cuff at the wrist" — so the generator did exactly what it was told, and the mismatch is between the NAME and the PROMPT, not between the prompt and the picture. The art itself is a clean success by every criterion: one object, centred, filling the frame, four or five large shapes, black-on-ember contrast that survives 15px. It is one of the more legible icons in the set.

Three reasons not to touch it. (1) It equips in the hands slot — the id is `ember_gloves`, `cslot:'gloves'` — so a hand covering is functionally the correct picture; the player sees a glove where their glove goes. (2) It is family-consistent: every hand-slot icon in the game is drawn as a hand covering (rough/chitin/wolf/ogre/troll/drake/demon/ember/void leather plus bronze/iron/mithril/runite/cobalt/gravesteel/barrow/moltensteel metal, ~17 icons). Silhouette-as-slot-cue is the strongest read the satchel grid has; breaking it for one tier would cost more legibility than it buys. (3) A literal bracer — an armless forearm tube — is a far worse 15px subject than a hand: with no fingers to give it scale it degrades into a bracelet, a scroll, or a log. Redrawing this would make it less recognisable, not more.

If Jordan wants the mismatch gone, the cheap and correct fix is one string at cindervale.html:26074 — change `gloves:'Bracers'` to `gloves:'Gloves'` (or 'Mitts'/'Grips'), which renames all nine leather tiers at once and makes 18 existing icons correct for free. Also note `lynx_bracers` (cindervale.html:26334) is a separate hand-slot item with the same naming, and its icon is likewise a glove. Re-running the art is the expensive way to fix a naming decision.

confirms.depicts: A complete spider in top-down view: bulbous abdomen, distinct cephalothorax, eight jointed legs radiating outward, plus raised front pedipalps (the emblem version adds two antenna-like spikes above the head). Solid near-black/dark plum silhouette with no interior detail. It is unmistakably a whole live arachnid, not a body part.
confirms.note: First pass is right, and this is not a borderline call. The prompt "A single dark segmented spider spinneret organ, fine bristles at the tip" hands Turbo the noun "spider" and it answered with its spider prior verbatim — "spinneret", "organ" and "bristles" all lost. Both __painted and __emblem show the same full eight-legged body; nothing in either frame reads as a gland, a tip, or a silk strand. At 15-20px the silhouette collapses to a black blob with eight radiating spikes, which is the single most recognisable shape in the whole icon set — a player will identify this as a spider monster or a spider trophy, not a harvested part. Worse, the library already leans on that shape: widow_crown is built from curling spider legs, and spider_silk / silkweave_band / silken_sigil cover the silk theme, so this drop collides with existing art instead of adding a distinct one. Fix requires dropping the noun entirely, per the ogre_hide lesson. Suggested rewrite (subject sentence only): "A single small dark segmented cone tapering to a blunt open tip, ringed with rows of fine stiff bristles, three pale silk threads trailing loose from the opening. Just the detached gland on its own — no legs, no eyes, no living creature." That gives a concrete shape to draw, states the absence positively, and never uses the word that caused the failure.

confirms.depicts: A small double-bitted hatchet: broad grey steel head with pale highlights on both bits, a short brown wooden haft with a rounded knob at the base, tilted at about 30 degrees. Head is roughly as wide as the haft is long.
confirms.note:
Confirmed, though not for the "no theming" reason alone — the hard failure is an icon collision. I rendered grave_cleaver next to the woodcutting tool line (iron_axe, steel_axe, bronze_axe) and next to its sibling 2H weapon forgebreaker. At full size grave_cleaver is iron_axe with a marginally darker haft: same double-bitted silhouette, same grey head, same brown wood, same tilt. Downscaled to the real 18px satchel size the two are indistinguishable — forgebreaker survives the same test only because its molten orange palette carries the whole read. So a player scanning the satchel does not see a boss-drop two-handed cleaver; they see the woodcutting hatchet they have been holding for hours. That clears the "would identify it as something else" bar.

Not wrong-object (it is an axe, and the item is an axe), hence weak rather than wrong-object.

Root cause is in the prompt, not the render: "A single huge two handed axe ... one broad blade at the top of a long haft" leads with the noun "axe", and Turbo answers that with its hatchet prior every time — "huge", "two handed" and "long haft" are exactly the qualifiers cfg 2.4 discards. Nothing in the prompt names grave, bone, rot or rust either, so the palette defaults to tool steel. The fix is to drop the noun "axe" entirely and change the reference class, plus give the shaft-to-head ratio something concrete to draw.

Suggested subject sentence: A single enormous headsman's cleaver on a long two handed shaft, the blade one broad rectangular slab of pitted grey iron taller than it is wide with a squared chopping edge and a hooked spike at the top corner, the shaft twice as long as the blade and bound in grey rag, bone grey metal streaked with grave rust and verdigris.
