Just the weapon standing upright — no hands, no wielder.

confirms.depicts: A pair of tall boots side by side seen from the front, charred near-black hide traced by a hard ember-orange rim light, with a bright ember glow sitting in the notch between the two boot shafts.
confirms.note: First pass overstated this. The shipped variant is emblem (picks.json). Downsampled to 15/16/20/31px on the dark panel: the rim light outlines the full boot silhouette and survives the downscale, so both shafts and the splayed feet stay legible at 20px and it is unmistakable at 31px. The glow is ~25% of frame width and ~6% of frame area, and it occupies the negative space BETWEEN the shafts, never covering the boot bodies. Peer check at 16px is decisive: it is more readable than wolf_boots__painted and troll_boots__painted (undifferentiated brown blobs) and far less glow-dominated than demon_boots__emblem, none of which were flagged. The centred glow is the shared emblem-variant treatment (demon/void/moltensteel/voidsteel boots) and is on-theme for an item named Emberhide. Only real nit: the small white-hot core plus the short white streak under it pull the eye and could be dimmed. Polish, not a defect. No prompt change needed.

confirms.depicts: A red creature head in profile — hooked snout, visible eye, swept-back crest — perched on top of an egg-shaped mass of dozens of overlapping diamond scales. At icon size it reads as a small dragon, or as a red pinecone. The emblem variant has no head but arranges the same scales into a symmetrical flower/rosette badge.
confirms.note: Confirmed. Item is "Wyrmscale", one raw scale drop; the icon is a creature plus a pile. Two independent misses: (1) "drake" in the prompt summoned a head, and (2) even the scaled body is a cluster, violating the one-object rule — the prompt never said how many. The word count is also far too low for Turbo to have anything specific to draw. Never use drake, dragon, or wyrm in the rewrite; "scale" alone is safe here because the shape description anchors it. Suggested rewrite: A single loose teardrop shaped scale, wide rounded top edge narrowing to a blunt point at the bottom, hard glossy bronze red surface with fine ridges fanning down its face and a thicker pale rim along the top edge, one flat scale lying by itself and filling the frame — no head, no face, no eyes, no living creature, just the one scale and not a cluster.

confirms.depicts: A keyhole. A glowing violet sphere sits on top of a downward-tapering black trapezoid body with a thin orange rim outline — circle-over-tapered-shaft is the textbook keyhole/lock silhouette. Nothing is burnt, broken, or lump-shaped.
confirms.note:
Confirmed, and not a judgement call — the silhouette is geometric and symmetrical (perfect circle joined to a straight-sided trapezoid), which is the opposite of what a cinder looks like. At 15-20px the orange rim reads as a keyhole plate and the violet sphere as a lit gem; a player would guess keyhole, lock, lightbulb or mushroom before "burnt ember". Prompt was "A single black cinder shot through with violet light" — no shape at all was described, so Turbo invented a symmetrical glowing form.

CHEAP FIX FIRST: the other variant is already correct-ish. C:/code/embervale/_iconart/cut/void_cinder__painted.png is an irregular rounded black chunk with a violet molten pool bleeding across the upper left — reads as a dark glowing lump, no keyhole. It is a bit soft/pebble-like (edges too smooth to say "burnt") but it is the right object. Flipping the entry in C:/code/embervale/_iconart/picks.json from "emblem" to "painted" fixes the wrong-object failure with zero regeneration.

If regenerating instead, drop the noun "cinder" (too vague for Turbo — it gave it a glow and no body) and lean on charcoal, which carries a strong correct prior, plus explicit broken geometry:

A single small lump of burnt charcoal, an angular chunk with sharp broken corners and flat chipped facets, deep jagged cracks splitting across it with violet light glowing up out of the cracks from inside. Just the one blackened chunk of rock, cooled and solid.

confirms.depicts: The shipped variant (picks.json selects "emblem") is a headless full suit of plate armour: a glowing orange cuirass with a neck cutout and flared pauldrons occupying the top third, a bent arm with a gauntlet hanging at the left hip, then dark legs with orange knee/ankle bands and boots below. The torso, not the legs, carries all the value contrast, so at 15px the icon reads as a bright orange chest-piece glow over a dark body. The unused "painted" variant is different and correct: legs from the hip down with a small belt, no torso, no arm.
confirms.note: Not a judgement call — the emblem literally draws a breastplate with pauldrons and an arm on top of the legs, and the glow puts the eye on the chest. The confusion is concrete rather than theoretical: emberforged_aegis in the same set is prompted "A single breastplate" and its emblem is also a dark silhouette with a glowing orange torso, so these two sit in the same grid reading as near-identical chest glows while one of them is leg armour. ember_chest / ember_legs are likewise "emblem" picks in the same family. Cheapest fix is no regeneration at all: flip picks.json emberforged_greaves from "emblem" to "painted" — that variant is hip-down leg armour with boots and reads as legs at 15px, only dimmer. If a regen is wanted instead, the prompt "A single pair of armoured leg greaves side by side" gives Turbo no upper boundary, so it completes the figure; state the absence positively and cut the body noun — e.g. "A single pair of armoured leg guards standing side by side, blackened iron banded with orange at the knee and ankle, cut off flat at the top of the thigh — just the empty leg casings and boots, no torso, no arms, no wearer."

confirms.depicts: A complete, intact, perfectly symmetrical gold crown — the painted version has three tapering points capped with gold balls, a diamond ornament at the centre front and an unbroken dark-rimmed band around the base; the emblem version is the same crown as a flat zigzag silhouette. There is no break, no torn edge, no missing stone anywhere in either file.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is more than cosmetic. The prompt did say "a single broken piece of a gold crown", but Turbo answered the noun "crown" with its stock whole-crown prior and dropped "broken piece" entirely — the same failure mode as ogre_hide. Two things make it worth a redraw rather than letting it pass as merely plain: (1) brokenness is the entire content of the name, so the icon states the opposite of what it labels; (2) the library already contains five genuine whole-crown items (lich_crown, rat_queen_crown, warchief_crown, widow_crown, chart_crown) and at 15-20px this symmetric crown blob is not distinguishable from any of them — the satchel gets five identical-silhouette entries, one of which is supposed to be a broken scrap. An asymmetric torn silhouette would actually read BETTER at that size, not worse. Suggested rewrite (drop "crown" as the head noun so it stops summoning the whole-crown prior; make the shard the subject and state the absence positively): "A single jagged shard of a gold headband, torn off along a ragged diagonal edge down the right side, with two bent triangular gold spikes still rising from the left end and one empty cracked stone socket between them. Just the one broken scrap of metal, curved but not a closed circle — no complete ring, no head wearing it."

confirms.depicts: A pair of knee-high brown leather riding boots, standing upright side by side, with full feet, rounded toe caps, heels, side buckles, and grey-white fur cuffs turned down at the top. No legs or wraps — these are complete footwear.
confirms.note: Item is "Wolfhide Chaps" (leg armour, gear family). The shipped picks.json variant is "painted", and that file is unambiguously boots — toe caps and heels are drawn at the bottom of both shafts. It is also a near-clone of wolf_boots__painted.png (same brown leather, same grey fur cuff, same paired-upright pose); at 15-20px in the satchel the two tiles are indistinguishable, so the player cannot tell chaps from boots. Cause: "shin guards ... knee down to ankle" is inside the boot prior's reference class, and "each ending in a flat straight cut edge at the bottom" was ignored as a qualifier. NOTE FOR THE FIX: wolf_legs__emblem.png is already correct — two footless leg wraps, knee to ankle, fur trim top and bottom, flat cut ends, no feet. Flipping picks.json from "painted" to "emblem" resolves this with no regeneration. If a repaint is wanted anyway, drop the words "shin guards" and "boot"-adjacent framing entirely and describe the object as two separate tapered hide leg wraps hanging side by side, cut off flat at the ankle with nothing below them, stating the absence positively: just the leg coverings — no feet, no toes, no heels, no footwear, no wearer.

confirms.depicts: A lumpy, cube-ish black mass with a hard crust, split by four large star-shaped orange fissures glowing from inside — a burning coal or cracked lava chunk. No fold, no drape, no frayed edge, no weave texture, no flat cloth plane anywhere in it.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and worse than the first pass called it — this is wrong-object, not merely weak. Emberweave is a fabric material; the icon is a solid mineral lump. picks.json selects "painted" for this id, so the lump is what ships. The failure is systematic, not a bad roll: the sibling voidweave ("A single folded square of near black cloth, violet rift light glowing between the threads") produced the exact same glowing-cube lump in violet, so the "folded square of cloth + light glowing between the threads" template is losing outright to the ember/charred prior. It also lands in the same visual bucket as the game's actual rock items — void_cinder and starfall_cinder are both black lumps with a glowing or cracked crust — so a player at 15px reads this as "another cinder", not cloth. Suggested rewrite that drops the losing nouns (no "ember", no "square", no "threads"): A single piece of soot-black woven fabric lying folded over on itself in three soft layers, the top corner turned back to show the underside, loose torn strings hanging off the lower edge, thin hot orange lines running along the creases of the folds. Just the limp flat fabric, soft and slack.

confirms.depicts: A maroon barrel-shaped mallet head on a long brown wooden handle running to the lower right, with a small dull-grey axe-like bit tucked underneath the head. It reads as a mallet or a gavel, not a cleaver.
confirms.note: First pass is right, and it is worse than "weak". The maroon cylindrical head is the largest, brightest and most saturated shape in the frame and it owns the silhouette; the grey blade is a low-contrast wedge hidden under it. Downsampled to 20px the blade collapses into what reads as the mallet's cast shadow, leaving a plain mallet-on-a-stick. The emblem silhouette is worse still: the blade merges into the head mass so the outline is a solid bulky-head-plus-thick-handle blob, i.e. a hammer/gavel with no cutting edge anywhere in the outline. A player in the satchel grid would call this a mallet, and it will not be told apart from any actual hammer icon in the set. Item name is "Crude Cleaver" (family drops3). Cause: the prompt describes the blade only in trailing qualifiers ("a rough rectangular iron blade with a chipped edge") while "crude ... rag wound grip" pulls a primitive-mallet prior, and at cfg 2.4 the prior wins. Fix by making the blade the whole object and giving it concrete edges, and by dropping "crude": "A single wide butcher chopping knife seen flat from the side, one large square cornered iron blade slab filling most of the frame with a straight flat top edge and a chipped straight cutting edge running along the bottom, a short rag wrapped stick handle at the right end, the whole tool flat and thin all the way through."

confirms.depicts: A correctly drawn small dagger, point down, pale grey-green blade, straight crossguard and a green gem pommel — but sitting on top of a large opaque saturated dark-green rounded-square plate that fills roughly half the frame and was never keyed out.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is a measurable defect rather than a taste call. Opaque-pixel fraction is 0.526 against 0.204 for gravesteel_sword and 0.241 for gravesteel_hammer — this dagger covers as much of the frame as gravesteel_shield (0.545). Every sibling gravesteel weapon is cleanly keyed to the object; this one alone retains a backdrop panel. picks.json selects "painted" for this id, so the broken file is the one that ships. Downsampled to 16 and 20 px over the satchel ground, the green plaque is the largest shape and the only saturated colour in the cell, so in a grid of transparent-background gear it reads as a green badge or tile rather than as a weapon; the dagger is only recoverable as a pale sliver once you already know to look for it. Held at "weak" rather than "unreadable" because the dagger itself is well formed and does resolve by ~31 px. The prompt is not at fault — it produced exactly the object asked for. The fault is the key step: the flat backdrop came out green, "tarnished grey green steel" pulled the whole field into the same hue band, and the keyer failed to separate them. Fix by re-keying, or by re-rolling on a backdrop hue outside green; changing the subject sentence alone will not help.

confirms.depicts: A fat-bodied black spider standing on eight splayed legs, with a small five-pointed crown perched on its back like a hat. The spider's body and leg span occupy roughly the lower two thirds and the full width of the frame; the crown is a separate small shape sitting on top of it, not a headpiece anyone could wear.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and it is the textbook failure mode: the prompt said "thin barbed spider legs curling up from the band" and the model answered the strongest noun, drawing a whole spider — same as ogre_hide producing an ogre. The item is a wearable crown (gear/head slot) but the icon is a live creature. The widest, highest-contrast shape in the frame is the leg span, so at 15-20px in the satchel grid this reads as a bug icon; the crown collapses into a bump on its back. The emblem variant is marginally better because the crown is gold against a black spider, but the composition is identical and the spider still dominates. Mitigating point I weighed and rejected: the item IS spider-themed, so an arachnid motif is not off-theme — but the object depicted is still an animal rather than the headpiece, and players will confuse it with the zone's spider monsters and pets. Fix direction: drop the word "spider" entirely, since it pulls the whole creature, and describe the band shape plus the absence positively. Suggested subject sentence: "A single black metal circlet with eight tall thin barbed spikes rising from the rim and curling inward over the top like hooks, seen from the front. Just the empty band standing alone — no head, no face, no body, no living creature."

confirms.depicts: A long thin black shaft laid corner-to-corner across the frame, with a small faceted violet crystal knob at the top end and a round ball at the bottom end. Reads as a sceptre, wand or light mace.
confirms.note: Confirmed at full resolution (file is native 128x128, not a downscale). The head-to-haft ratio is inverted from a hammer: the violet knob is about a quarter of the shaft length and barely wider than the haft itself, while the shaft runs the full diagonal. A hammer's whole silhouette signal is a massive block head on a short stubby handle, and none of that is present. At the 15-20px satchel size this reduces to a diagonal line with a bead on it, which a player would read as a sceptre or staff, not a hammer. The prompt is not at fault - "one huge square head at the top, short thick handle" is already the concrete-shape phrasing that works, and Turbo simply answered the rod prior. Verified the first pass's other claim: recol_cut/voidsteel_hammer__painted.png is a correct sledgehammer (wide flat-topped rectangular violet head, short stout haft, round pommel) that is unmistakable at any size. Fix is to repoint the sheet at that cut rather than regenerate.

confirms.depicts: A fitted black long-sleeved top: full sleeves running to cuffs at the wrists, rounded padded shoulder caps, a pinched waist and a flared scalloped hem, with an orange ember glow pooling at the collar and bleeding down the shoulder seams. No plate edges, no rivets, no cuirass silhouette — it reads as a cloth or leather bodice/blouse.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and the fix is already on disk. The item is defined at cindervale.html:26449 as PLATE-class chest armour, Lv70 tier 3 — "Aegis" plus "Emberforged" both promise forged metal. The shipped icon has sleeves with cuffs and a corseted waist with a flared hem; a breastplate has neither. At 20px it is a dark torso blob with an orange collar glow, which a player reads as a robe or tunic, and it is out of step with emberforged_greaves in the same set, which clearly reads as armoured legs with orange trim. IMPORTANT: emberforged_aegis__painted.png is correct — a proper blackened plate cuirass with pauldrons, articulated arm plates and a four-pointed ember star on the chest. picks.json currently maps "emberforged_aegis": "emblem"; flipping that one entry to "painted" and re-running inject fixes this with no regeneration. If regeneration is wanted anyway, drop the word "breastplate" (it drew a garment) and give it shape: "A single hollow chest piece of blackened iron, a rigid curved front plate with a raised ridge down the centre, thick riveted rims at the neck and armholes, two heavy rounded shoulder guards, cracks across the plate glowing hot orange. Just the empty shell standing upright — no arms, no sleeves, no cloth, no wearer."

confirms.depicts: A cartoon long limb bone (femur/humerus) lying on a diagonal — pale cream, swollen lobed joint knobs at BOTH ends, tapering shaft between. The emblem variant is the same limb-bone shape with a row of dark hatch marks across the shaft. No flat plate, no thin arc, no rib form anywhere in either version.
confirms.note:
Confirmed, and the collision is verified rather than suspected. I upscaled rib_plate__painted and put it beside the other bone drops in the same library: ancient_bone__painted and gnawed_bone__painted are the same off-white knobbed dog-bone silhouette, same palette, same diagonal. At 15-20px in the satchel a player reads all three as one picture and would name this "Ancient Bone" before "Rib Plate". So this is not merely plain art — it is the wrong bone AND a duplicate of two live items.

Cause: the source prompt "A single curved plate of pale rib bone, ridged along its length" let the noun "bone" pull the model's generic-bone prior; "plate", "rib" and "ridged" were all dropped. Note the word "rib" is also risky in the other direction (rack of ribs / meat), so the rewrite should avoid leaning on it as the head noun.

Suggested rewrite, shape-first with the knobs excluded positively and the reference class changed away from "bone":
"A single long slender arc of pale cream horn, broad and thick at the wide end and tapering evenly to a narrow blunt tip at the other, bending in one smooth crescent curve, its flat outer face crossed by shallow parallel grooves. Both ends are plain cut stubs — smooth, flat and narrow, with no round joint balls, no lobes and no swelling at either tip."

confirms.depicts: A taut kidney/bean-shaped green gland with a heavy dark rim, one large glossy specular highlight upper-left, and a soft internal tonal gradient — a sealed, glistening organic sac.
confirms.note: Over-flag. The icon depicts the correct object: a venom sac is a sealed taut gland, and a smooth glossy blob is what one looks like — nothing here reads as a different item. Pixel stats on the painted file (128x128) show real value structure, not a flat fill: 3721 dark rim/shadow px against 5641 mid-green px, so it holds a bold dark-rimmed silhouette against the dark UI at 15px, which is exactly the property that survives at that size. The first pass's prescribed fixes (membrane veining, a duct, a bead of fluid at the tip) are sub-pixel at 15-20px and would read as noise inside the shape rather than as detail. The "indistinguishable from any other green material" claim also fails on inspection: I searched every audit-*.json and the library contains exactly one other green blob, ectoplasm ("translucent pale green, dripping"), which renders as a pale washed green with a ragged fringe of drip tendrils along its base — different value and different silhouette from this deep-green dark-rimmed bean. The smoothness is arguably the correct read, since a sac is intact while ectoplasm is spilled; adding a drip would erode the distinction that currently exists. Legitimate but minor polish notes, below the bar for a rework: the green is louder/more lime than the dark-fantasy palette used elsewhere, and a slightly pinched neck at the top would sharpen the silhouette. The __emblem variant is much flatter (75% of its opaque area in a single colour bucket) so if either version is ever reworked it is that one, not the painted sheet version.

confirms.depicts: A lumpy irregular dark-red organic mass with a near-black rim and two hot orange-yellow glowing cores with soft halos inside it — a lump of flesh lit from within.
confirms.note: Shipping variant is painted (picks.json: cinder_gland -> "painted"), which is what the first pass saw. It is not the wrong object: the item is "Cinder Gland" and the icon is a dark red fleshy lump with hot orange light glowing inside it, which is the item, plainly. Not unreadable either — I box-downsampled it to 15px and the silhouette holds as a defined lumpy round mass, with luminance running 10 to 132 and both bright cores surviving as distinct spots rather than smearing into one wash. The "reads the same as any other red material" claim does not hold up when tested against its actual satchel neighbours: void_cinder and starfall_cinder cap at luminance 53-54 and downsample to flat featureless discs, brimstone and venom_sac are far brighter and visibly textured, molten_bar is a diagonal bar. cinder_gland is in fact the only one in that group that reads as a dark body with two hot cores, so it is differentiated rather than confusable. The fair criticism is that it lacks any gland-specific structure — no neck, membrane, or vessels — so it is generic rather than unmistakable. That is plain, not wrong, and the player-recognition bar is met. Worth passing along as a cheap upgrade rather than a defect: the already-generated cinder_gland__emblem.png is the better picture and needs no regeneration, only a picks.json flip. It has exactly the shape the first pass asked for — a pinched neck at the top over a bulging lower lobe, with an internal orange glow column running down the middle — and better contrast (peak luminance 153 vs 132) at 15px.

confirms.depicts: A double-bitted battle axe: two dark grey crescent blades with bright sharpened silver edges meeting at the top of a straight brown wooden haft with a rounded pommel. No stone or boulder anywhere; the emblem version is the same axe silhouette in flat navy.
confirms.note: Genuine failure, and the prompt caused it. The prompt opens with "A single huge two handed axe" and says "one broad blade at the top of a long haft" before asking for a boulder "instead of a blade" -- Turbo answered the strongest noun (axe) plus the reinforced noun (blade) and discarded the correction. Item data confirms the mismatch: troll_maul is dmgType:'crush' with a stun proc, its own desc reads "A boulder lashed to an ironwood haft", and the legacy SVG at cindervale.html:12060 draws a lumpy boulder head. The painted icon reads as a slashing axe and collides with the woodcutting/battle-axe icons already in the library. Fix by removing the words axe, blade and weapon entirely and leading with the stone as the subject. Suggested: "A single huge rough grey boulder lashed with thick leather cords to the top of one long straight dark wooden pole, the lumpy stone head wide and round and heavier on one side, the bare pole running down from it to a wrapped grip -- just stone and wood, no edge, no metal, no point."

confirms.depicts: A pair of upright emerald-green armoured leg plates standing side by side, each with a rounded knee guard near the top, a riveted vertical seam down the shin, and a small sabaton foot at the base.
confirms.note: First pass is mistaken about the specific failure. Rendered both this icon and runite_boots at 18px and 31px and set them side by side: the silhouettes are not close. Runite Legs is two tall narrow columns filling the frame top-to-bottom with only a slight flare at the base; Runite Boots is a squat, bottom-heavy mass in the lower two-thirds with a broad cuff and large bulbous feet. Aspect ratio and mass distribution — the only cues that survive downscaling — differ sharply, and the emblem variants separate even harder (thin strokes vs fat L-shapes). The sabaton is a few pixels at satchel size and does not drive the silhouette. Fair remaining criticism is that these read as greaves rather than platelegs (no waist joint), but that is a plainness quibble, not a misidentification: a player sees green leg armour and reads leg armour.

confirms.depicts: A gold maul head on a short haft, with a disembodied gold fist and forearm — knuckles, thumb and a wrist cuff all legible at 4x — closed around the haft below the head.
confirms.note: Confirmed, and the first pass understated it: the lower mass is not a garbled form, it is an unmistakable severed hand gripping the shaft, complete with a forearm stub and cuff. It breaks the pipeline's own "no hands holding it" rule. Because the hand is the exact same pale gold as the weapon, it never reads as a separate element — at 31px the bottom half is a knobby gold knot with no visible haft, and at 15-16px it is pure mush. Not wrong-object: the head is a clean, legible hammer at every size, so a player will still call it a maul; the icon is identifiable but poor, hence "weak" not "unreadable". Root cause is the prompt "A single huge two handed maul, one colossal pale gold block on a long haft" — "two handed" is a noun-adjacent hand cue that Turbo answered literally by drawing a hand, and "long haft" got no shape description to compete with it. A rewrite should drop the phrase "two handed" entirely, describe the haft concretely (a plain straight wrapped shaft with a rounded pommel at the base), and state the absence positively: just the weapon lying alone, no hand, no arm, no wielder. The __emblem variant of this same icon is already clean — a correct maul silhouette with no hand — so swapping the pick for this id is the zero-cost fix if a regeneration is not wanted.

confirms.depicts: A bright saturated gold boot. Flat-topped shaft down the left, a heel spur kicking out bottom-left, and a rounded toe curving away to the right at the bottom, with hard specular streaks that read as polished metal. Mean opaque RGB 218/167/21 with the blue channel near zero across the entire object, so no ivory, cream or bone value is present anywhere. There is no taper: the far end is as thick as the shaft and blunt-rounded. At 16-31px it snaps to "golden boot", and the same drop family already ships ogre_boots as a grey pair of boots, so a player would read this as a boot variant rather than a tusk.
confirms.note: Live pick is the painted variant (picks.json: "ogre_tusk": "painted"). The word "yellowed" drove the full-saturation gold, and "curved ... tapering to a blunt point" produced a hook with no taper. Drop "yellowed" and "blunt" entirely, name ivory as the material, put the wide end at the bottom and the point at the top so the taper has a direction, and rule out the animal positively. Suggested prompt: A single long ivory tusk standing upright, a thick cracked chalky cream root spreading wide at the bottom, narrowing smoothly and evenly all the way up to a fine sharp point at the top, dull off white with dark brown staining across the lower third. Just the loose bare tusk by itself, no animal, no skull, no jaw, no metal.

confirms.depicts: A lit torch or lamp post: a long thin dark violet pole topped by a small bell/cone-shaped shade that tapers inward toward the pole, glowing violet inside with a bright orange cap at the very top. Nothing blunt, square or hammer-like.
confirms.note:
Judged the emblem variant, which is the one that ships — C:/code/embervale/_iconart/picks.json has "riftcrusher": "emblem". Measured on the 128px source: head is only 32px wide against an 8px haft and, worse, it TAPERS INWARD as it meets the haft (a lampshade/flame silhouette), where a hammer head must be a blunt block meeting the haft at a right angle. The orange cap on top reads unambiguously as flame. At 31px it is a street lamp; at 16px the thin haft sinks into the panel and only an orange-violet dot survives. A player would name this a torch or a lantern staff, not the war hammer "Riftcrusher".

The first pass's stated reason is partly wrong — the head is 4x the haft width, not "barely wider" — but the verdict is right, and its severity is too lenient: this is a different object, not a plain one.

CHEAPEST FIX, no regeneration needed: C:/code/embervale/_iconart/cut/riftcrusher__painted.png is already a good icon. It is a proper war maul — a big rounded-square block head 46px wide (2.3x its 20px haft), squared off where it meets the haft, with a bulbous pommel and a bright violet gem caged in the head face. It reads as a maul at 31px and still holds a hammer silhouette at 16px. Flip picks.json to "painted" for this id.

If regeneration is preferred instead, the failure is that "war hammer" plus "violet light" let Turbo answer with its torch prior. Drop the glow language from the silhouette description and make the head's width and squareness the loudest thing in the sentence, e.g.: A single heavy maul lying head-up, one massive squared iron block at the top three times as wide as the shaft it sits on, flat blunt faces on both sides of the block, a short thick shaft below it ending in a round knob, a small violet gem set in the centre of the block face.

confirms.depicts: A green heater shield seen face on — flat top, tapering to a point at the bottom, faceted emerald face with a small round boss at the centre and three rivets. Not a small round buckler.
confirms.note: Confirmed, but as "weak" not "wrong-object": it is a shield, and a buckler is a shield, so the class is right and the runite green is right. What makes it a real defect rather than a plain icon is the collision. I checked picks.json — the live variant for both runite_buckler and runite_shield is __painted, and side by side at 20px the two are the same green heater silhouette; the buckler's boss reads as a single lighter pixel and the shield's centre highlight reads as a vertical streak. A player scanning the satchel or an offhand comparison would take one for the other. The defining trait of the item — small and round — is absent entirely. This is systemic across the family: iron_buckler and steel_buckler are heater shields too, because the noun "shield" carries the heater prior at cfg 2.4 and "a small round buckler" is a qualifier it ignores (steel_buckler also came out red-and-chrome despite "bright silver steel", the same known shield prior). Fix by removing the word shield from the prompt entirely and describing the disc: something like "A single small round metal disc the width of a hand, seen face on, one domed rivet at its exact centre and a ring of small rivets around the outer edge, rich emerald green runite" — no "shield", no "buckler", no "boss".

confirms.depicts: A single dark leather glove filling the frame, five blunt digits, a wide cuff at the wrist banded in bright violet, with an ember-orange glow washing down the fingers into black.
confirms.note: First pass over-flagged. The prompt asked for "a single soft leather glove, fingers curled, wide cuff at the wrist" and that is exactly what the icon shows: a bold, clean glove silhouette with an unmistakable cuff and violet band, the strongest-contrast shape in the frame. The claim that "the glove itself is barely legible against the hand shape" is a misread - there is no hand in the picture, no skin tone, no wrist stump, no arm. The glove is the entire silhouette, and it reads as a glove down to 15px. On the orange: picks.json ships the emblem variant, and the same ember glow spilling from the garment's opening is present on void_boots (emblem, shipped) and void_legs (emblem, shipped), plus void_chest's emblem. It is a deliberate Voidhide-tier family signature, not a colour failure on this one icon. Violet-only would arguably suit the name better - that is a polish preference, and changing only the gloves would break the set's visual consistency. A pure black/violet alternate does exist at void_gloves__painted.png if the theme is ever unified across the whole set, but nothing here is wrong enough to warrant a regen.

confirms.depicts: An upright sword with a near-black violet blade, light lavender highlight bevels along both cutting edges, a black crossguard, wrapped grip and round pommel.
confirms.note: First pass has the colour backwards. The painted icon is a dark blade with light violet edges, which is exactly the prompt's "black blade with a thin violet cutting edge" — not a light blade with a dark core. Measured mean colour over opaque pixels: voidedge 55,42,69 (dark violet) vs voidcleaver 45,29,65 (its sibling, near-identical) vs steel_sword 162,162,163 (light, hueless grey). Voidedge is about 3x darker than the Steel Sword and strongly hue-shifted, so the "indistinguishable at 15px" claim fails; I downsampled both to 15/20/31px and Voidedge reads as a vertical purple blade with a black hilt while Steel Sword reads as a diagonal white-outlined grey blade. The only real quibble is that the lavender bevels are brighter and wider than "thin", so at sheet scale the highlight catches the eye before the black core — a highlight-weight nitpick, not a wrong object. Silhouette is the cleanest of the three void weapons on the sheet. Separately: voidedge__emblem.png (unused on this sheet) does have an orange/copper blade with only a violet rim, which would be off-name if that variant were ever swapped in.
